INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA
  Wednesday, September 23, 2026
  Open Session – 2:00 p.m.

  Web Sites:
  www.cityofinglewood.org/1680/Long-Term-Rentals

  SPECIAL MEETING

  NOTICE AND CALL OF SPECIAL MEETING OF THE INGLEWOOD
  RENTAL HOUSING BOARD
  (Government Code Section 54956)

  TO THE MEMBERS OF THE INGLEWOOD RENTAL HOUSING BOARD

 NOTICE IS HEREBY ORDERED by the Chairperson that a special meeting of the Rental Housing
 Board will be held on Wednesday, September 23, 2026, at 2:00 P.M., in the Council Chambers, One
 Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood, California (Government Code Section 54956).

  *****NOTE FROM THE CITY*****

The doors to the Council Chamber on the 9th Floor will open at 1:40 p.m. for Open Session. Please be
mindful that seating is limited and available on a first-come, first-served basis.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the Rental Housing Board by sending them to the Rental Housing Board
Secretary at rentalhousingboard@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Rental
Housing Board prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the
meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number and/or subject matter.
Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 a.m. and
prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact
the Office of the Housing Protection Board at (310) 412-4330 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities
Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation
thereof. Any person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or translation services
in order to observe and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation,
or service by contacting the Housing Protection Department by telephone at 310-412-4330, FAX at 310-412-
4276, One Manchester Boulevard, Suite 602, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email to
rentalhousingboard@cityofinglewood.org no later than 48 hours prior to the scheduled meeting.

 The City of Inglewood Rental Housing Board held a meeting on Wednesday, November 12, 2025,
in the Council Chambers located in City Hall of said city.

Chairperson Heaney called the Rental Housing Board meeting to order at the hour of 2:05 p.m.,
followed by the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our country.
The Rental Housing Board Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
Present: Chairperson Heaney, Rental Housing Board Members Hamilton, Fragoso, Evans,
and Brown.
City officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Yakema Decatur  Housing Services Director/ Assistant City Manager
  Qiana Lowe  Housing Services, Long-Term Rental Deputy Director
  Amari Watson  Rental Housing Board Liaison
  NeCosia James  Rental Housing Board Secretary
  Shatara Smith  Rental Housing Board Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.
Chairperson Heaney inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the Rental
Housing Board on any item on the agenda other than the capital improvement petitions.
There were no responses.
Chairperson Heaney closed public comment at the hour of 2:07pm.
CONFLICT OF INTEREST DECLARATION.
The Rental Housing Board Secretary took roll to confirm there were no conflicts of interest with
any item on the agenda. The roll call was as follows:

Ayes: Rental Housing Board Member Evans; and
Noes: Rental Housing Board Members Hamilton, Fragoso, Brown, and Chairperson Heaney.

Chairperson Heaney duly noted that Board Member Evans would recuse herself from deliberating
and voting on agenda item No. 5 for the property located at 218 N. Locust Inglewood, CA 90301
(Case No. 25-O-0003).
MINUTES – APPROVED
The Rental Housing Board Secretary announced item No. 2, approval of the minutes for the
meeting held on October 8, 2025.

It was moved by Chairperson Heaney, seconded by Board Member Hamilton, that the minutes of
the Rental Housing Board meeting held on October 8, 2025, be approved. The motion was carried
by the following roll call vote:

Ayes: Rental Housing Board Members Hamilton, Fragoso, Brown, Evans, and Chairperson
  Heaney; and
Noes: None.
 HEARING HELD- CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PETITION - ROOF REPLACEMENT AT 934 LARCH STREET. The
Rental Housing Board Secretary announced item No. 3, a Capital Improvement Petition submitted by Allen
Gozini, on behalf of Morzini LLC, for the property located at 934 Larch Street, Inglewood, California 90301
(Case  No.  25-O-0001).
Chairperson Heaney inquired if notice of the hearing had been provided to the applicant and
tenants. The Board Secretary confirmed notice.
Amari Watson, Rental Housing Board Liaison, presented a brief synopsis of the petition explaining
that the owner is seeking reimbursement of the cost associated with a roof replacement at a total
of $70,000.00.
Chairperson Heaney inquired if the applicant was present to address the board.
Speaker Gio Felix, representative of Morzini LLC, spoke explaining that the property has 3 floors,
the top floor was leaking, this had resulted in mold developing and dry wall collapsing within some
tenant units, the leaking had even reached the second floor level. He stated that the replacement of
the roof was critical to prevent further deterioration.
Chairperson Heaney inquired if any Board Members had any comments.

Board Member Hamilton inquired about the total number of units at the property. He confirmed
that there are 20 units, and noted that the owner was requesting reimbursement for only 15 of those
units. Board Member Hamilton asked the representative why reimbursement was being requested
for only 15 units.

Mr. Felix explained that certain conditions, including collapsing areas, were present only in
specific units and the remaining five units were located on the ground floor and were not affected.

Board Member Brown inquired when the previous roof had been installed.

Mr. Felix stated that the roof had not been replaced since the building was built in 1964.

Board Member Hamilton inquired whether roof patching had been performed prior to the roof
replacement.

Mr. Felix explained that the previous roof was flat, which allowed water to accumulate on the roof
and cause damage. He stated that the flat roof was completely removed and replaced with a new
roofing system consisting of tar and sealant, along with drainage outlets that now allow water to
flow off the roof rather than collect on top.

Board Member Hamilton inquired whether the roof had been removed down to the plywood.

Mr. Felix affirmed that the existing roof had been removed to the plywood, new plywood had been
installed, and the roof had been rebuilt.

Board Member Brown inquired when ownership of the property was acquired and asked whether
the roof had been inspected prior to ownership of the property in 2024. She further inquired
whether the roof inspection had passed at that time.
 Mr. Felix stated that he was unable to confirm whether the inspection had passed because he wasn’t
the manager at the time, he has been in management position for only six months. He did confirm
that an inspection was completed.

Chairperson Heaney inquired whether there were any public comment for item NO. 3.

No Response.
Chairperson Heaney closed the public comment portion at the hour of 2:16 p.m., and recessed the
meeting for deliberation.
Chairperson Heaney called the meeting back into order at the hour of 2:55 p.m.
Ms. Decatur returned as the secretary announcing a quorum was present.
Following deliberation, it was moved by Board Member Hamilton and seconded by Board
Member Brown that the Rental Housing Board does hereby approve the eligible reimbursement of
$26,250.00 for 15 units at $48.61 each month for 36 Months effective February 1, 2026.
The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Rental Housing Board Members Hamilton, Fragoso, Brown, Evans, and Chairperson
Heaney; and
Noes: None.

HEARING HELD- CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PETITION - REPAVING DRIVEWAY
AT 627 W. QUEEN ST. The Rental Housing Board Secretary, James, announced item No. 4, a
Capital Improvement Petition submitted by Susan Yamato for the property located at 627 W.
Queen Street, Inglewood, CA 90301 (Case No. 25-O-0002).

Chairperson Heaney inquired if notice of the hearing had been provided to the applicant and
tenants. The Board Secretary confirmed notice.
Amari Watson, Rental Housing Board Liaison, presented a brief synopsis of the petition,
explaining that the applicant was seeking reimbursement for the cost of repaving the driveway and
carport with concrete at a total cost of $16,000.00. She explained that the property contains seven
units, six of which are eligible for the capital improvement pass-through.
Chairperson Heaney inquired if the applicant was present to address the board.
Applicant Susan Yamato addressed the board regarding Case No. 25-O-0002 and provided an
explanation for the completed improvement.
Chairperson Heaney inquired if there were any public comments
Speaker Detra Hall in Unit 1 spoke, stating that the work constituted as deferred maintenance
rather than a capital improvement and explained that the owner has a history of delaying repairs
and is now attempting to make tenants pay when it becomes urgent.
Chairperson Heaney inquired if any Board Members had any questions or comments.
 There were no response.
The Applicant addressed the Board in response to the comments made during public comment,
stating that she maintains her property and provides quality housing for her tenants. She explained
that the asphalt had deteriorated to the point where tenants had expressed concerns, and rather than
continuing to make temporary repairs, she decided to replace it in its entirety.
Chairperson Heaney closed the public comment portion of the hearing at the hour of 3:03 p.m. and
recessed the meeting for board deliberation.
Chairperson Heaney called the meeting back into order at the hour of 3:31p.m.
Ms. Decatur returned as the secretary, and announced a quorum was present.
Following deliberation, it was moved by Board Member Hamilton, and seconded by Board
Member Fragoso that the Rental Housing Board does hereby approve the eligible reimbursement
of $6,857.16 for 6 units at $31.75 each month for 36 Months effective February 1, 2026.
The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Rental Housing Board Members Hamilton, Fragoso, Brown, Evans, and Chairperson
  Heaney; and
Noes: None.

Upon Chairperson Heaney’s request, Board Member Evans recused herself from the
discussion, left the Dias, and did not participate in the next hearing.
HEARING HELD- CAPTIAL IMPROVEMENT PETITION FOR REPLACING ENTIRE
ELECTRICAL SYSTEM AT 218 N. LOCUST The Rental Housing Board Secretary, James,
announced item No. 5, a Capital Improvement Petition submitted by Julia and Willie Jordan, on
behalf of 218 Locust LLC for the property located at 218 N. Locust Street, Inglewood, California
90301 (Case No. 25-O-0003).

Chairperson Heaney inquired if notice of the hearing had been provided to the applicant and
tenants. The Board Secretary confirmed notice.
Amari Watson, Rental Housing Board Liaison, presented a brief synopsis of the petition, stating
that the applicant was seeking reimbursement for the cost of replacing the property's entire
electrical system, at a total cost of $97,920.00. The property contains four units, three of which are
eligible for the capital improvement pass-through. Ms. Watson explained that while the total
project cost was $97,920.00, only $28,800.00 is eligible for reimbursement.
Chairperson Heaney inquired if the applicant was present to address the board.
Applicant Julia Jordan addressed the Rental Housing Board regarding this matter, and provided an
explanation for the completed improvement.

Chairperson Heaney inquired if any Board Members had any comments.
 Board Member Hamilton inquired whether the property owner's insurance company had required
the replacement of the electrical system.

The applicant Mrs. Jordan, responded that it had not.

Board Member Hamilton also inquired if the electrical updates were completed in each unit on the
property.

The applicant affirmed.

Board Member Brown asked whether there had been any electrical issues prior to the replacement.

The applicant stated that there had been no known electrical issues; however, the original
manufacturer of the electrical system was no longer in business, and the system, which had been
in place since the property was constructed in the 1950s, would eventually require replacement.
The applicant stated that the replacement was completed proactively rather than in response to an
existing electrical issue.

Chairperson Heaney confirmed the number of units on the property to be four, inquiring if there is
also a laundry room, and an office unit.

The applicant affirmed.

Chairperson Heaney then opened the hearing for public comment.

There was no response.
Chairperson Heaney closed public comment and called the meeting into recess for deliberation at
the hour of 3:42pm.
Chairperson Heaney called the meeting back into order at the hour of 4:29 p.m.
Board Member Evans returned to the Dias.
Ms. James returned as Board Secretary and announced a quorum was present.
Following deliberation, it was moved by Board member Hamilton and seconded by Board member
Brown that the Rental Housing Board does hereby approve the reimbursement of $12,960.00 for
3 units at $60.00 each month for 72 Months effective February 1, 2026.
The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Rental Housing Board Members Hamilton, Fragoso, Brown, and Chairperson Heaney;
Noes: None; and
Abstain: Rental Housing Board Member Evans.

REQUEST FOR REVISIONS OF DOCUMENT – REVISE OWNER PETITION The Rental
Housing Board Secretary James announced item No. 6, a request to revise the owner petition for
capital improvements as previously voted upon by the Rental Housing Board.
 It was moved by Board Member Fragoso and seconded by Board Member Hamilton that the Rental
Housing Board does hereby approve the revision of the owner’s petition for capital improvements.
The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Rental Housing Board Members Hamilton, Fragoso, Brown, Evans, and Chairperson
Heaney; and
Noes: None.

REQUEST FOR REVISIONS OF DOCUMENT – REVISE LETTER OF INTENT FOR
CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS. The Rental Housing Board Secretary, James, announced item
No. 7, a proposal to revise the Letter of Intent for Capital Improvement’s pass-through fee notice.

Amari Watson, Rental Housing Board Liaison, presented a brief synopsis regarding a revision to
the Letter of Intent for Capital Improvement Pass-Through Fees. She noted that revisions were
made to page 2 of the Letter of Intent document, where the revised language now states: “A capital
improvement pass-through shall not apply to rental units or new tenants whose initial rent was
established after the completion of the improvement.” The change clarifies that eligibility for the
capital improvement pass-through fee is based on the completion date of the improvement, rather
than the date the petition was filed.

It was moved by Board Member Hamilton and seconded by Board Member Brown that the Rental
Housing Board does hereby approve the revised language of the Letter of Intent for Capital
Improvement Pass-Through Fees. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Rental Housing Board Members Hamilton, Fragoso, Brown, Evans, and Chairperson
Heaney; and
Noes: None.

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING OTHER MATTERS. Chairperson Heaney inquired
whether there were any persons present wishing to address the Rental Housing Board on any matter
related to the City of Inglewood Housing Protection regulations other than items listed on the
agenda.

There was no response.

Chairperson Heaney advised that individuals with complaints should submit them to the Housing
Protection Department Director for review and resolution.

Chairperson Heaney closed the public comment period

CHAIRPERSON AND BOARD MEMBER REMARKS. Chairperson Heaney inquired
whether the Rental Housing Board had any additional comments.

There were no comments.

There being no further business, Chairperson Heaney adjourned the Rental Housing Board meeting
at the hour of 4:34 p.m.
 Approved this ________ day of _____________, 2026.

Chairperson Heaney called the Rental Housing Board meeting to order at the hour of 2:08 p.m.,
followed by the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our country.
The Rental Housing Board Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
Present: Chairperson Heaney, Rental Housing Board Members Hamilton, Fragoso, and
Evans.
City officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Yakema Decatur  Housing Services Director/ Assistant City Manager
  Amari Watson  Rental Housing Board Liaison
  NeCosia James  Rental Housing Board Secretary
  Shatara Smith  Rental Housing Board Assistant

Yakema Decatur acted as Board Secretary.

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.
Chairperson Heaney inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the Rental
Housing Board on any item on the agenda other than the capital improvement petitions.
There were no responses.
Chairperson Heaney closed public comment at the hour of 2:10 pm.
CONFLICT OF INTEREST DECLARATION
The Rental Housing Board Secretary took roll to confirm there were no conflicts of interest with
any item on the agenda. The roll call was as follows:

Ayes: None; and
Noes: Rental Housing Board Members Hamilton, Fragoso, Evans, and Chairperson Heaney.

 HEARING HELD - CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PETITION - ROOF REPLACEMENT
AT 948 S INGLEWOOD AVE. The Rental Housing Board Secretary announced item No. 2, a
Capital Improvement Petition submitted by Yaakov Greenspan c/o Westland Real Estate Group,
for the property located at 948 S. Inglewood Ave., Inglewood, California 90301 (Case No. 25-O-
0004).

Chairperson Heaney inquired if notice of the hearing had been provided to the applicant and tenants. The
Board Secretary confirmed notice.
Amari Watson, Rental Housing Board Liaison, presented a brief synopsis of the petition, stating that the
applicant was seeking reimbursement for the cost of a roof replacement, at a total cost of $108,340.30. The
property contains twenty-two units. Ms. Watson explained that while the total project cost was $108,340.30,
only $54,170.15 is eligible for reimbursement.
 Chairperson Heaney inquired if the applicant was present to address the board.
Representative of Westland Real Estate Group, Katherine Schoerner addressed the Rental Housing Board
regarding this matter and explained that the roof was replaced to prevent tenants from continuing to
experience recurring issues. She further stated that the new roof was installed using higher-quality materials
than the previous roof.
Chairperson Heaney inquired if there were any public comments
The tenant residing in Unit 17 addressed the Rental Housing Board, stating that she believed the roof
replacement was not a capital improvement but rather a necessary repair resulting from failed maintenance.
She stated that she moved into the building in 2021 and had submitted requests to address roof leaks. The
tenant further stated that the leaks had caused swollen wood panels, peeling paint, and mold growth within
her unit. She expressed her belief that the work performed was a repair rather than an improvement. The
tenant provided pictures and videos to the Rental Housing Board in support of her comments.

Ryna Duvet, the tenant residing in Unit 12, addressed the Rental Housing Board and stated that he
moved into the property in 2018 and has experienced numerous maintenance concerns. He
provided photographs, videos, and documentation to the Board in support of his statements.

Mr. Duvet stated that rain entered his apartment in 2018, at which time he submitted a maintenance
request. He further stated that he continued to submit maintenance requests and emails regarding
the issue in 2021, 2022, and 2023. According to Mr. Duvet, the leaking was most severe during
the current year, with water entering through the light fixture and windows. He also stated that
mushrooms had grown from the ceiling and that portions of the ceiling appeared brown and moldy.
Mr. Duvet expressed his belief that the roof replacement did not constitute as a capital
improvement.

Board Member Hamilton asked the property representative whether multiple bids had been
obtained for the roof work.

Katherine confirmed that bids had been obtained.

Chairperson Heaney confirmed with the representative that the work was completed in 2024.

Katherine further stated that, to her knowledge, there had been no additional maintenance concerns
following the roof repair. She explained that management would only become aware of such
concerns if tenants submitted maintenance requests.

Board Member Hamilton asked the tenant residing in Unit 17 whether her unit was still
experiencing leaks. The tenant confirmed that she had observed leaking around her window the
previous night. She acknowledged that conditions had improved since 2021 but stated that leaks
were still occurring.

Board Member Hamilton asked whether she had notified management of the recent leaking. The
tenant stated that she intended to submit a maintenance request that day regarding the leak from
the previous night. She further stated that she had documentation of maintenance requests
previously submitted to management.
 Board Member Hamilton confirmed with the tenant that the leaks occurred after the completion of
the improvement, and the tenant confirmed that they had.

Board Member Hamilton asked Mr. Duvet whether he would like to comment on the effect of the
previous night’s rain on his unit. Mr. Duvet stated that the rainfall had not been heavy and that he
had not observed any leaks. However, he explained that leaks generally do not become visible
until after one or two days of rain. He also stated that maintenance had repaired a leak in his unit
the previous week that resulted from rainfall that occurred a few weeks ago.

The tenant residing in Unit 17 spoke again in support of Mr. Duvet’s statements.

Chairperson Heaney closed the public comment portion of the hearing and recessed the meeting
at 2:24 p.m.

Chairperson Heaney called the meeting back into order at the hour of 3: 00 p.m.
The Board Secretary announced a quorum was present.
Following deliberation, it was moved by Chairperson Heaney, and seconded by Board Member Hamilton,
that Case No. 25-O-0004 does not meet the criteria of a capital improvement, which states that the new
improvement must have a useful life of 5 years or more.
The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes: Rental Housing Board Members Hamilton, Evans, Fragoso, and Chairperson
  Heaney;
Noes: None; and
Abstain: Rental Housing Board Member Fragoso.

HEARING HELD - CAPTIAL IMPROVEMENT PETITION FOR ROOF
REPLACEMENT AT 827 W BEACH. The Rental Housing Board Secretary announced item
No. 3 , a Capital Improvement Petition submitted by Yaakov Greenspan c/o Westland Real Estate
Group, for the property located at 827 W. Beach Ave., Inglewood, California 90302 (Case No. 25-
O-0005).

Chairperson Heaney inquired if notice of the hearing had been provided to the applicant and tenants. The
Board Secretary confirmed notice.
Amari Watson, Rental Housing Board Liaison, presented a brief synopsis of the petition, stating that the
applicant was seeking reimbursement for the cost of a roof replacement, at a total cost of $43,187.00. The
property contains eleven units. Ms. Watson explained that while the total project cost was $43,187.00, only
$21,593.50 is eligible for reimbursement.

Chairperson Heaney inquired whether the applicant was present to address the Rental Housing
Board.

Katherine Schoerner, representing Westland Real Estate Group, addressed the Rental Housing
Board regarding the matter. She explained that the project involved a complete roof replacement,
including the removal of the existing roof and the installation of a durable four-ply gravel roof
 system. Ms. Schoerner stated that the improvement provides tenants with a safer and more
structurally sound living environment.

Chairperson Heaney inquired whether there were any members of the public who wished to
address the Rental Housing Board regarding the matter.

No response.

Board Member Hamilton asked Ms. Schoerner to confirm the date the capital improvement was
completed.

Ms. Schoerner stated that the project was completed in March 2024.

Board Member Fragoso inquired about the definition of a re-roof and the difference between a
roof replacement and a roof repair.

 Ms. Schoerner explained that a re-roof involves removing and replacing the entire roof system
down to the underlying structure, whereas a roof repair consists of repairing only specific portions
of the roof.

Chairperson Heaney inquired whether any tenants had responded to the hearing notice.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Amari Watson confirmed that no tenant responses had been
received.

Chairperson Heaney closed the public comment portion of the hearing and recessed the meeting
at 3:02 p.m.

Chairperson Heaney called the meeting back into order at the hour of 3: 29 p.m.
The Board Secretary announced a quorum was present.
Following deliberation, it was moved by and seconded by Board Member Fragoso, that the applicant re-
serve the Letter of Intent, and that the matter be continued to the March 11, 2026, Rental Housing Board
meeting due to the owner's failure to provide the Letter of Intent to the Housing Protection Department at
the time the Capital Improvement Petition was submitted.
The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes: Rental Housing Board Members Hamilton, Evans, Fragoso, and Chairperson
  Heaney; and
Noes: None.

HEARING HELD - CAPTIAL IMPROVEMENT PETITION FOR ROOF
REPLACEMENT AT 812 E HYDE PARK. The Rental Housing Board Secretary announced
item No. 4 , a Capital Improvement Petition submitted by Yaakov Greenspan c/o Westland Real
Estate Group, for the property located at 812 E Hyde Park Blvd., Inglewood, California 90302
(Case No. 25-O-0006).
 Chairperson Heaney inquired if notice of the hearing had been provided to the applicant and tenants. The
Board Secretary confirmed notice.

Chairperson Heaney inquired if a Letter of Intent was submitted when the petition was submitted.

Board Liaison Amari Watson stated no.

It was moved by Chairperson Heaney, and seconded by Board Member Hamilton, that the
applicant re-serve the Letter of Intent and that the matter be continued to the March 11, 2026,
Rental Housing Board meeting due to the owner's failure to provide the Letter of Intent to the
Housing Protection Department at the time the Capital Improvement Petition was submitted.

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes: Rental Housing Board Members Hamilton, Evans, Fragoso, and Chairperson
  Heaney; and
Noes: None.

PUBLIC COMMENT

Chairperson Heaney inquired if there was public comment.
Representative Katherine argued that she did provide the Letter of Intent.
The Board Secretary explained that staff verified the Letter of Intent was submitted after the Capital
Improvement Petition had been filed, despite the requirement that it be submitted with the petition.
Chairperson Heaney closed public comment at the hour of 3:33p.m.

CHAIRPERSON AND BOARD MEMBER REMARKS. Chairperson Heaney inquired
whether the Rental Housing Board had any additional comments.

There were no comments.

There being no further business, Chairperson Heaney adjourned the Rental Housing Board meeting
at the hour of 3:34 p.m.

Approved this ________ day of _____________, 2026.

HEARING HELD- APPEAL OF HEARING OFFICER’S DECISION RE: REDUCTION
IN HOUISNG SERVICES (GARAGE REMOVAL) AT 124. N. INGLEWOOD AVE.
INGLEWOOD, CA 90301. The Rental Housing Board Secretary announced Agenda Item No. 2,
an Appeal Application submitted by property owner Jonathan Gallagher regarding a Hearing
Officer's decision involving a reduction in housing services resulting from the removal of tenant
garages at 124 N. Inglewood Avenue, Inglewood, California 90301 (Case No. 25-T-0003-A01).

Chairperson Heaney confirmed with the Board Secretary that notice of the hearing had been given
to the appellant and affected tenants. The Board Secretary confirmed that notice had been given.
 Chairperson Heaney introduced herself, the members of the Rental Housing Board, City staff, and
the City Attorney. She then provided an overview of the purpose of the appeal hearing, explaining
that the Board's role was to determine whether substantial evidence supported the Hearing Officer's
decision regarding the rent reduction petition for the property. Chairperson Heaney further
explained the hearing procedures, advising that the Board's review would be limited to the
evidence previously submitted into the record, that no new evidence would be accepted, and that
Board Members could ask questions of the parties before deliberating and rendering a decision.

Amari Watson, Rental Housing Board Liaison, presented a brief synopsis of the matter. She
explained that the appeal was filed by the property owner following the Hearing Officer's
determination that the removal of the garages constituted a reduction in housing services
warranting a monthly rent reduction of $400.00 per affected tenant. She noted that the owner was
exercising the right to appeal that decision.

Chairperson Heaney opened the hearing for the appellant to speak.

Property owner Jonathan Gallagher, accompanied by Gill Ezequiel stated that they agreed a rent
reduction was appropriate, but believed the Hearing Officer's determination of $400.00 per month
was excessive. They explained that they offered a monthly rent reduction of $150.00 based on
local parking costs and calculations related to the size and square footage of the garage area, which
they estimated represented approximately 25 percent of the garage value. They further stated that
the City had issued permits authorizing the construction project and that they believed they had
received conflicting messages regarding the removal of the garages. They also maintained that the
leases stated the garages were intended for parking rather than storage and that they intended to
restore parking spaces for three of the units upon completion of the ADU project.

Chairperson Heaney then invited testimony from the tenants in support of the Hearing Officer's
decision.

Tenant Maro Lopez stated that tenants were required to remove their vehicles and personal
property from the garages with the understanding that parking would be restored following
construction. He stated that only three parking spaces would be available upon completion, despite
four existing garages being removed. Mr. Lopez further testified that shelving within the garages
led tenants to reasonably believe storage was permitted and explained that he now incurs a monthly
storage expense of $275.00. He also described the hardships experienced by tenants due to the loss
of parking, including changes to work schedules, difficulty locating street parking, and financial
impacts resulting from reduced work hours. Mr. Lopez submitted his lease agreement in support
of his testimony.

Tenant France Maldonado stated that she had resided at the property since 2001 and had always
been provided a garage. She testified that the loss of parking has caused safety concerns because
she must now park on the street at night. She further stated that after discontinuing rented parking,
her vehicle was broken into and that she lost the ability to store personal belongings previously
kept in the garage. Ms. Maldonado also stated that the garage locks had been removed and
submitted photographs in support of her testimony.
 Tenant Isabel, Unit 5, commented that she had resided at the property since 1995 and had
historically used the garage for storage. She stated that the removal of the garage created
difficulties finding parking, limited her ability to visit family due to parking concerns, and created
hardships for her disabled husband, who now must walk longer distances. She stated that she
currently pays $125.00 per month for a storage unit that is smaller than the former garage. Ms.
Isabel further testified that this hearing was the first time she became aware that only three parking
spaces would be restored and stated that she had not been offered a rent reduction. She also
indicated that the property owner blamed the garage removal on the City's approval of the ADU
project.

Tenant Hugo, Unit 5, stated that he is disabled and that the loss of garage parking has created a
significant hardship because he is now required to park on the street and walk greater distances.

Chairperson Heaney then asked whether the appellant wished to respond to the tenants' testimony.

Gill responded on behalf of the owner, acknowledging that the tenants had experienced
inconvenience. He stated that the owners had attempted to construct underground parking to
replace the garages but were unable to do so because the City did not approve that proposal.

Board Member Hamilton confirmed with the owners that only three parking spaces would be
available after construction and inquired how those spaces would be assigned. The owners
responded that one of the tenants who testified did not regularly park on the property.

Board Member Hamilton reviewed the lease language regarding storage and noted that the rules
concerning storage appeared unclear. The owners responded by describing the deteriorated
condition and age of the garages and explained that the structures had been converted into
accessory dwelling units.

Board Member Hamilton asked tenant France Maldonado about her statement regarding the
removal of the garage locks. Ms. Maldonado clarified that an individual driving a black truck
removed the locks and stated that she doesn’t believe it was the property owners who physically
removed them.

Board Member Hamilton asked whether tenants had received notice before their property was
removed. Mr. Gallagher stated that tenants were provided 60 days' notice, followed by an
additional week, before the locks were removed.

Tenant Isabel then read a text message she had received from the property owner, stating that the
notice period provided to tenants was shorter than represented and asserting that the locks had been
removed earlier than indicated.

Board Member Fragoso asked the owners to explain how they determined that a $150.00 monthly
reduction was appropriate. He then asked whether either party wished to provide any additional
information as to why the Board should or should not uphold the Hearing Officer's decision.

No additional comments were offered.
 Legal Counsel Gabriel advised the Board that its responsibility on appeal was to determine whether
substantial evidence supported the Hearing Officer's findings and decision based upon the existing
administrative record.

Chairperson Heaney asked whether Board Member Evans had any questions.

No response.

Chairperson Heaney then invited comments from Board Member Brown.

Board Member Brown asked whether the owners had informed tenants that storage was prohibited
in the garages. She noted that the garages were included as part of the tenancy and questioned the
owners regarding their treatment of the tenants' belongings after the locks were removed. She
further confirmed with the owners that they viewed the garages solely as parking spaces but had
not clearly communicated that storage was prohibited with tenants.

Chairperson Heaney inquired whether rents would be restored if parking was eventually reinstated.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Amari Watson explained that the Hearing Officer's decision
addressed the present reduction in housing services and was not based on the future restoration of
parking.

The City Attorney further clarified that the tenant petition before the Hearing Officer addressed
the current loss of parking and related housing services rather than any future replacement of
parking. He explained that the Hearing Officer considered the overall loss experienced by tenants,
including the loss of secure parking, storage, and the additional burdens associated with locating
street parking.

Board Member Hamilton requested clarification regarding the owners' proposed 25 percent
reduction compared to the Hearing Officer's $400.00 monthly reduction.

The City Attorney explained that the Hearing Officer rejected the owner's proposed calculation
after evaluating the evidence and determining that the methodology, which relied primarily on the
garage square footage, did not accurately reflect the value of the lost housing service. He further
explained that the Hearing Officer instead relied on a methodology supported by an RSG study,
along with an additional valuation formula, to determine that a monthly rent reduction of $400.00
was appropriate.

Attorney Gary Rhoades addressed the Board and stated that the Hearing Officer's written decision
contained the evidence relied upon in reaching the determination. He noted that the Hearing
Officer awarded an amount that was lower than the amount suggested by the study.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Amari Watson provided additional background regarding the tenant
petition and the owner's proposed 25 percent reduction.
 Following deliberation, Chairperson Heaney moved to affirm and uphold the Hearing Officer's
decision. The motion was seconded by Board Member Evans.

The motion carried by the following vote:

Ayes: Rental Housing Board Members Fragoso, Evans, Brown, and Chairperson Heaney;
Noes: None; and
Abstain: Rental Housing Board Member Hamilton.
